problem: The exponents are lost, so the displayed arithmetic is false. Section 3 reads "The Hamming bound for t = 1 is 2n−k ≥ 1 + n. For (7,4): 23 = 8 and 1 + 7 = 8", and Q6 reads "23 ≥ 1 + 7". "23 = 8" is not true, and "2n−k" can be misread as 2n − k.
fix: Use superscripts: "The Hamming bound for t = 1 is 2<sup>n−k</sup> ≥ 1 + n. For (7,4): 2<sup>3</sup> = 8 and 1 + 7 = 8." In Q6: "For t = 1 the Hamming bound gives 2<sup>3</sup> ≥ 1 + 7, and 8 = 8."

problem: "each output bit is the modulo-2 sum of the G columns marked by m" is wrong twice: the encoder XORs the rows of G picked by the 1 bits of m, and that XOR gives the whole codeword, not one output bit. Bit j of c is the sum of the entries in column j of the selected rows. A student who follows the text will build the wrong wiring.
fix: Write: "the encoder XORs the rows of G marked by the 1 bits of m; bit j of the codeword is the modulo-2 sum of the entries in column j of those rows."
